title: Preparing a Brochure or Catalog for Print: A Buyer's Checklist
h1: Preparing a brochure or catalog for print: a buyer's checklist
description: Prepare a brochure or catalog project: purpose, format and folds, final content, images, page count, print specs, bleed, proofs and digital versions.
intro: Brochures and catalogs are still valuable sales tools, from trade shows to product ranges and service menus. Print projects, however, punish late changes and missing details. A wrong fold, low-resolution photo or text placed too close to the edge can mean reprinting the whole run. This article explains what to decide and prepare before hiring a designer, and what to check before anything goes to the printer.

faq.a: Extra image area beyond the trim line, so colors and photos reach the edge cleanly after cutting.

faq.q: What file does the printer need?
faq.a: Usually a print-ready PDF with bleed, crop marks and the correct color settings.

faq.q: Should I order a printed proof?
faq.a: For large or color-critical runs, yes. Screen colors can differ from printed colors.

faq.q: Can the same design work as a PDF online?
faq.a: Yes, but ask for a separate screen-optimized version with working links.
